issues.label: Juvenile court jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm subject-matter and personal jurisdiction over the juvenile and offenses.

issues.label: Proper charging instruments
issues.why: Court must ensure complaints/citation complied with Juv.R. and provided adequate notice of alleged acts.

issues.label: Traffic citation refiling validity
issues.why: Court must determine legal effect of dismissal/refiling of jaywalking citation including timeliness and procedural regularity.

issues.label: Statute of limitations
issues.why: Court must confirm all charges were filed within applicable limitation periods.

issues.label: Venue in Hamilton County
issues.why: Court must ensure offenses were committed in the county or otherwise properly venued.

issues.label: Address discrepancies materiality
issues.why: Court must decide whether inconsistent offense locations undermine probable cause, proof, or notice.

issues.label: Suppression standard of review
issues.why: Court must separate factual findings (deference) from legal conclusions (de novo) when reviewing suppression ruling.

issues.label: Credibility and fact findings
issues.why: Court must resolve conflicts in testimony and make findings supporting suppression decision.

issues.label: Initial encounter type
issues.why: Court must classify police conduct as consensual encounter, investigatory stop, or arrest to apply correct constitutional standard.

issues.label: Reasonable suspicion for stop
issues.why: Court must decide whether officers had reasonable suspicion to stop K.J. for jaywalking or weapons-related indicators.

issues.label: Probable cause for jaywalking stop
issues.why: Court must determine whether observed jaywalking created probable cause to detain/cite and what scope of detention was lawful.

issues.label: Reliance on radio dispatch
issues.why: Court must apply collective-knowledge doctrine to whether uniformed officers could rely on Davis/Kress observations.

issues.label: High-crime area factor
issues.why: Court must decide how much weight to give “high crime area” in the totality-of-circumstances analysis.

issues.label: ShotSpotter relevance
issues.why: Court must assess whether ShotSpotter context contributed to suspicion or was an improper generalized justification.

issues.label: Flight as suspicion
issues.why: Court must determine whether unprovoked flight elevated suspicion and whether flight alone supports seizure/arrest.

issues.label: When seizure occurred
issues.why: Court must decide the moment K.J. was seized (if ever before custody) under Fourth Amendment standards.

issues.label: Obstruction probable cause
issues.why: Court must determine whether K.J.’s conduct met elements of obstructing and provided probable cause to arrest.

issues.label: Lawfulness of police act
issues.why: Obstructing requires a “lawful” act by the officer, so court must decide if attempted stop was lawful.

issues.label: Right to avoid police
issues.why: Court must consider constitutional limits on criminalizing refusal to cooperate or walking/running away absent lawful detention.

issues.label: Use of threats/taser
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether threatened force affected seizure analysis or rendered conduct unlawful/excessive.

issues.label: Hot pursuit entry issues
issues.why: Court must determine legality of any warrantless entry or intrusion into apartment/common areas during pursuit.

issues.label: Standing/privacy in apartment
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. had a reasonable expectation of privacy to challenge any apartment search.

issues.label: Third-party consent
issues.why: If officers searched based on an occupant’s permission, court must evaluate voluntariness and scope of consent.

issues.label: Search warrant requirement
issues.why: Court must decide whether a warrant was required for the apartment/closet search and whether an exception applied.

issues.label: Exigent circumstances
issues.why: Court must assess whether exigency (e.g., hot pursuit, destruction of evidence, officer safety) justified a warrantless search.

issues.label: Protective sweep limits
issues.why: If search was framed as a protective sweep, court must ensure it was justified and properly limited in scope.

issues.label: Abandonment doctrine
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. abandoned any property (bag/gun) by fleeing/placing it, affecting Fourth Amendment protection.

issues.label: Plain view/plain feel
issues.why: Court must determine whether officers lawfully accessed the area and immediately recognized contraband to seize it without a warrant.

issues.label: Scope of search of containers
issues.why: Finding a gun in a lunch box/closet raises whether opening containers exceeded lawful scope absent a warrant/exception.

issues.label: Inevitable discovery
issues.why: If search legality is questionable, court must consider whether evidence would have been discovered lawfully anyway.

issues.label: Attenuation from illegality
issues.why: If initial stop/arrest was unlawful, court must analyze whether later evidence was sufficiently attenuated to be admissible.

issues.label: Fruit of poisonous tree
issues.why: Court must decide whether gun, statements, and DNA were derived from any unconstitutional seizure/search.

issues.label: Miranda custody/interrogation
issues.why: Court must determine whether K.J.’s statements at the station followed proper Miranda warnings and waiver.

issues.label: Juvenile Miranda safeguards
issues.why: Court must consider heightened scrutiny for juvenile waivers (age, comprehension, voluntariness, presence of parent/guardian if applicable).

issues.label: Voluntariness of confession
issues.why: Court must ensure statements were not coerced under Due Process totality-of-circumstances.

issues.label: Sixth Amendment attachment
issues.why: Court must determine if right to counsel had attached at questioning and whether any violation occurred.

issues.label: DNA collection legality
issues.why: Court must assess whether collecting K.J.’s DNA was authorized and constitutional for a juvenile in this posture.

issues.label: Chain of custody gun
issues.why: Court must ensure the firearm was properly handled, identified, and linked to the case for admissibility.

issues.label: Operability proof
issues.why: For “deadly weapon” firearm issues, court must confirm operability evidence (test-fire) satisfies statutory requirements.

issues.label: Sufficiency standard delinquency
issues.why: Court must apply criminal-law sufficiency (Jackson v. Virginia) to adjudications beyond a reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Manifest weight standard
issues.why: Court must apply manifest-weight review (factfinder credibility/weight) to the jaywalking finding as raised.

issues.label: Concealed weapon elements
issues.why: Court must decide whether evidence proved K.J. knowingly had a concealed deadly weapon on/near his person.

issues.label: Concealment nexus to person
issues.why: Court must determine whether weapon in apartment closet can support “concealed on person or ready at hand” at relevant time.

issues.label: Knowledge/possession of gun
issues.why: Court must decide whether evidence showed K.J. actually or constructively possessed the firearm.

issues.label: Constructive possession factors
issues.why: Court must evaluate proximity, dominion/control, access, and admissions to link K.J. to gun in shared apartment.

issues.label: Crossbody bag inference
issues.why: Court must determine whether bag observations support carrying/concealment or are speculative without contents observed.

issues.label: Tampering elements
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. altered/destroyed/concealed evidence with purpose to impair its value/availability.

issues.label: Pending investigation knowledge
issues.why: Tampering requires knowledge of an official proceeding/investigation likely, so court must assess whether flight/pursuit suffices.

issues.label: Purpose to impair evidence
issues.why: Court must determine whether hiding gun in closet/lunch box shows specific purpose to impair availability.

issues.label: Obstructing elements
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J., without privilege, hampered/impeded a public official in official duties.

issues.label: Substantial hindrance
issues.why: Obstruction requires an actual hindrance, so court must assess whether chase/diversion constituted substantial interference.

issues.label: Privilege or justification
issues.why: Court must consider whether any legal privilege (e.g., avoiding unlawful stop) negates obstructing culpability.

issues.label: Jaywalking ordinance elements
issues.why: Court must determine what CMC 506.46 requires (e.g., outside crosswalk/when crosswalk present) and whether proved.

issues.label: Proof of jaywalking act
issues.why: Court must assess whether admissible evidence established K.J. crossed unlawfully, including reliance on Davis’s observation.

issues.label: Citation witness competency
issues.why: Court must address whether citing officer’s lack of personal observation affects the traffic adjudication.

issues.label: Multiplicity allied offenses
issues.why: Court must consider whether carrying concealed weapon and tampering/obstructing merge or are separately punishable in juvenile context.

issues.label: Dismissed charges impact
issues.why: Court must ensure burglary/RSP dismissals do not prejudice findings or admit improper other-acts evidence.

issues.label: Other-acts evidence limits
issues.why: Court must ensure references to high-crime area/other guns/drugs do not become inadmissible propensity evidence.

issues.label: Marijuana relevance/prejudice
issues.why: Court must consider whether marijuana evidence was admissible for context or unfairly prejudicial.

issues.label: Evidentiary admissibility rules
issues.why: Court must ensure testimony and physical evidence met Ohio Rules of Evidence as applicable in juvenile adjudications.

issues.label: Hearsay at suppression vs trial
issues.why: Court must distinguish permissible hearsay use at suppression from stricter trial admissibility requirements.

issues.label: Identification of K.J.
issues.why: Court must ensure witnesses reliably identified K.J. as the individual who jaywalked, fled, and entered the apartment.

issues.label: Causation timeline clarity
issues.why: Court must reconcile sequence (jaywalk, approach, flight, entry, search, recovery) to apply legal standards correctly.

issues.label: Due process notice/fairness
issues.why: Court must ensure K.J. received fair notice of allegations and an opportunity to be heard at each stage.

issues.label: Right to counsel
issues.why: Court must confirm K.J. had counsel (or valid waiver) at critical stages including suppression and adjudication.

issues.label: Confrontation rights
issues.why: Court must ensure K.J. could cross-examine adverse witnesses at adjudication consistent with due process/Confrontation Clause.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: Court must apply correct burdens: state’s burden at adjudication; defendant’s initial burden and state’s burden on exceptions at suppression.

issues.label: Findings on record
issues.why: Court must provide sufficient reasoning/factual findings to permit meaningful appellate review, especially on suppression.

issues.label: Disposition legality
issues.why: Court must ensure DYS commitment/suspension and conditions were authorized and proportionate under juvenile statutes.

issues.label: Stay-away order authority
issues.why: Court must confirm authority and reasonableness for no-contact/stay-away condition through 2029.

issues.label: Credit/time limits of control
issues.why: Court must ensure the term “until age 21” and any probation/suspended commitment comply with statutory maximums.

issues.label: Costs/indigency determination
issues.why: Court must confirm proper indigency finding and lawful remission of costs.

issues.label: Collateral consequences advisements
issues.why: Court must ensure any required advisements (firearm disability, records, DNA) were given where mandated.

issues.label: Double jeopardy concerns
issues.why: Court must ensure refiling and multiple adjudications do not violate double jeopardy protections.
